top_cited_works.title: Reynolds number and slant angle effects on the flow over a slanted cylinder afterbody
top_cited_works.abstract: The cylinder with a slanted base is a simplified, canonical bluff body geometry that shares similarities to aircraft fuselages, which are known to produce a strong vortex pair due to their upswept afterbody. This work will examine in detail the surface flow and near-field characteristics of the flow over the slanted cylinder for slant angles of , where the formation of either a separated wake flow state or a vortex-dominated flow state is dependent upon initial conditions, i.e. the presence of overshoot of the free-stream velocity during wind tunnel start-up.

recent_works.title: Three-Dimensional Flow Topology of Double-Fin Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction Using Volumetric Velocity Measurements
recent_works.abstract: Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction (SBLI) poses inherent challenges for supersonic/hypersonic aircraft, including flow separation, unsteady pressure loading, vibration, and engine unstart. A symmetric Double-Fin is a canonical configuration often used in high-speed aircraft components and subsystems, such as vertical tails and ramjet/scramjet inlets. Experiments to investigate SBLI induced by Double-Fin with fin angles of 10 ∘ , 12 ∘ , and 15 ∘ , resulting in increasingly stronger interactions, are conducted at Mach 2. Using Scanning-Stereoscopic Particle Image Velocimetry (S-SPIV), three-dimensional, three-component velocity fields are acquired, facilitating a deeper exploration of highly three-dimensional multi-shock interactions. The evolution of this complex flow, such as the interaction of λ -shocks generated by the fins, is comprehensively examined for improved understanding of the governing flow physics. In particular, the interaction between the front-foot of the reflected-shock and the fin-shock gives rise to a distinct, stronger shock referred to as Shock-Tangle , accompanied by a localized low-velocity region. recent_works.title: Volumetric Experimental Characterization and Validation of a Supersonic Dual-Stream Rectangular Jet
recent_works.abstract: A dual-stream supersonic rectangular jet is experimentally investigated using a scanning stereo particle imaging technique to capture the three-dimensional velocity flow fields. The nozzle features a supersonic core stream and a sonic bypass stream, separated by an internal splitter plate, which interact downstream of the throat. The experimental results are compared to high-fidelity numerical simulations to validate the measurement methodology for complex supersonic flows. The volumetric reconstruction reveals previously unreported details of the jet’s evolution, including the presence of mixed inflow and outflow counter-rotating corner vortices and their influence on the jet plume shape and shear layer development. The results provide new insight into the complex three-dimensional flow physics of dual-stream rectangular nozzles, and demonstrate the capability of this volumetric experimental technique to capture key features of supersonic flows that are difficult to observe with traditional planar measurements.

recent_works.title: High-Resolution, Quantitative Density Tomography Using a Rotating Nozzle
recent_works.abstract: In this work, we will demonstrate the Telecentric Rotating Nozzle Background Oriented Schlieren (TRON-BOS) technique at Syracuse University's Skytop Facility to perform density reconstructions through BOS with 1,200 nozzle views over the course of a short ($\sim$1 minute) scan for several flows of interest to propulsion with intricate projections that make density tomography typically challenging but are resolved through the use of a large number of views. The results of our technique are compared to RANS simulations as a reference with limited region of validity. Comparisons between speckle-background BOS and filtered checkerboard demodulation BOS are performed to understand the trade-offs between resolution and accuracy for select cases. We also examine the loss in accuracy as less views are used to assess the minimum number of views required for a reconstruction, which is in the order of 300 views with full 360$^\circ$ observation of the density field. recent_works.abstract: This dataset is a companion data to the publication "High-resolution, quantitative density tomography using a rotating nozzle" by Zigunov, Wagner and Namatsaliuk (AIAA Scitech 2026). (Manuscript Here) The algorithm used is based on the mathematical formulation detailed in "Time-averaged density tomography of non-axisymmetric jets with a rotating nozzle and telecentric, single-camera BOS" by Zigunov (ExIF 2025). (Manuscript Here) It also serves as a companion dataset for the open-source code (also here) to perform the volumetric reconstruction based on raw images/vector fields.
